source_quote: In his complaint submitted to the Cyber Crime Station (CCS) Malkajgiri
note: The420.in: 'registered with the Malkajgiri cybercrime police'; ETV Bharat Telugu: 'మల్కాజ్‌గిరి పోలీసు సైబర్ క్రైం పోలీసులకు ఫిర్యాదు చేశారు'. Newsmeter says Neredmet police (Neredmet is in the Malkajgiri commissionerate; v1 row C36). Tag correct.

claim: The prefrontal cortex handles logic, planning and checking whether something is right (on-screen: PREFRONTAL CORTEX · ILLUSTRATION)
source_quote: These PFC regions extensively interconnect to regulate higher-order decision making and to plan and organize for the future.
note: Same review: 'The PFC also monitors errors, giving us the insight that we are incorrect and need to shift strategies'.

claim: Yale neuroscientist Amy Arnsten: stress we cannot control, even mild, rapidly and dramatically impairs prefrontal function (on-screen: [ARNSTEN | NATURE REVIEWS NEUROSCIENCE, 2009])
source_quote: Even quite mild acute uncontrollable stress can cause a rapid and dramatic loss of prefrontal cognitive abilities
note: Arnsten AF, 'Stress signalling pathways that impair prefrontal cortex structure and function', Nat Rev Neurosci 2009;10(6):410-422, PMID 19455173. Affiliation: 'Department of Neurobiology, Yale University School of Medicine'. It is a loss of function (reversible), not physical damage: the VO's పనితీరుని దెబ్బతీస్తుంది (hits its functioning) is right.

claim: Mainstream view: acute stress impairs working memory and cognitive flexibility, with mixed effects on inhibition
source_quote: We found that stress impaired working memory and cognitive flexibility, whereas it had nuanced effects on inhibition.
note: Shields, Sazma & Yonelinas, Neurosci Biobehav Rev 2016 (meta-analysis, PMID 27371161); effects were moderated by other variables such as sex. Supports the film's claim in simplified form; not every thinking skill fails.

claim: Feeling in control protects against the effect; feeling out of control is what impairs
source_quote: Subjects who felt in control of the situation (even if this was an illusion) were often not impaired by stress exposure, whereas those who felt out of control were impaired
note: Arnsten 2009. Fits the VO's 'stress we cannot control' and the film's advice to break the isolation.

claim: Days on end of threats, surveillance and fear (23 Feb to 2 Mar)
source_quote: kept under psychological pressure by the fraudsters for several days before transferring large sums of money
note: Fixed 2026-10-09 per fact-check: wording now matches the reports. "several days" of pressure (The420.in, 9 Mar 2026); video-call surveillance (Newsmeter, 9 Mar 2026). The ordeal spans 23 Feb to 2 Mar (8 days), but no report says the fear or surveillance was continuous; reports say 'several days' of pressure and video-call confinement with no duration. REPLACEMENT te: ఇప్పుడు ఆలోచించండి. ఒక గంట కాదు, ఒక రోజు కాదు. రోజుల తరబడి, బెదిరింపులు, నిఘా, భయం. ఆ స్థితిలో చదువు, హోదా, అనుభవం, ఏదీ పనిచేయదు. అది వాళ్ళ బలహీనత కాదు. అది మెదడు బయాలజీ. en: Now think. Not one hour, not one day. Days on end of threats, surveillance and fear. In that state, education, status, experience, none of it works. That isn't their weakness. That's the biology of the brain. Picture: do not run the REC counter as DAY 1 to DAY 8 of continuous recording; show the calendar 23 FEB to 2 MAR, or keep RECONSTRUCTION on the counter.

claim: In that state education, status and experience do not protect you; it is brain biology, not weakness
source_quote: People from every class and age group fall victim to Digital Arrest.
note: PM in Mann Ki Baat, 27 Oct 2024 (IANS). Science rows: Arnsten 2009, Shields 2016. 'None of it works' is stronger than the lab evidence. OPTIONAL te: ఆ స్థితిలో చదువు, హోదా, అనుభవం కూడా మనల్ని కాపాడలేకపోవచ్చు. en: In that state, even education, status and experience may not protect us.

claim: They target elders and respected people
source_quote: indicating a pattern of organized criminal activity targeting senior citizens.
note: Supreme Court order, 17 Oct 2025. ETV Bharat Telugu 21 Mar 2026: 'ప్రధానంగా డిజిటల్ అరెస్ట్ కేసుల్లో వృద్ధులు, విశ్రాంత ఉద్యోగులే టార్గెట్‌గా'. The reputation reason is the TGCSB SP's point (V038 row).

claim: MHA warned the gangs use studios made to look like police stations and government offices, and wear uniforms (on-screen: [MHA / I4C ALERT | MAY 2024])
source_quote: The fraudsters are known to use studios modelled on Police Stations and Government offices and wear uniforms to appear genuine,
note: MHA alert, 14 May 2024 (ETV Bharat, 14 May 2024). The Sentinel, 15 May 2024: '...and wear uniforms to appear genuine, alerts the MHA.'

claim: In Ambala, Haryana, an elderly couple was shown Supreme Court-named orders with judges' forged signatures (on-screen: AMBALA [SUPREME COURT SUO MOTU ORDER | 17 OCT 2025])
source_quote: The fraudsters displayed forged orders of the Supreme Court through WhatsApp and video conferencing. ... A "Surveillance Order" with forged judicial signatures
note: The order speaks of 'judicial orders bearing forged signatures of Judges'; FIRs at 'Cyber Crime Branch, Ambala'. The Leaflet: 'a senior citizen couple from Ambala, Haryana, who were defrauded of ₹1.05 crore'.

claim: They lost over Rs 1.05 crore (on-screen: ₹1.05 CR+)
source_quote: the victims were coerced to transfer Rs.1,05,50,000 through multiple bank transactions.
note: Rs 1,05,50,000 = over Rs 1.05 crore. Some outlets misprinted Rs 1.5 crore.

claim: The Supreme Court was aghast; fake court orders attack public trust in the justice system
source_quote: We are, however, aghast at the fact that the fraudsters have fabricated judicial orders in the name of the Supreme Court of India ... strikes at the very foundation of public trust in the judicial system
note: Order of 17 Oct 2025 (Justices Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi). The VO's ఆశ్చర్యపోయింది (astonished) is milder than 'aghast'. OPTIONAL: నివ్వెరపోయింది (was stunned).

claim: The Supreme Court took up the case suo motu in October 2025 (on-screen: SUO MOTU · OCT 2025 [SUPREME COURT OF INDIA])
source_quote: SUO MOTO WRIT PETITION (CRIMINAL) No(s).3/2025 ... Date : 17-10-2025
note: In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents.

claim: Oswal was put through a fake Supreme Court hearing on Skype, with the fake judge using the then-CJI's name (on-screen: SIMULATION · FAKE COURTROOM [BAR & BENCH | 2024])
source_quote: staged a fake virtual courtroom, with one of them impersonating Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud
note: TNM 2 Oct 2024: 'fake Supreme Court hearing via Skype with a fake judge who posed as CJI Chandrachud'. Never show the real CJI's face.

claim: He said he could not see the face but heard a gavel
source_quote: Though I could not see his face, I could hear him talking and banging a hammer on the table.
note: Oswal to The Indian Express, quoted by TNM and Bar & Bench. సుత్తి (hammer) matches.

claim: Camera on 24 hours; Oswal was told to keep Skype on even while asleep (on-screen: PILLAR 2 · ISOLATION · REC ● 47:12:09)
source_quote: they instructed me to keep Skype in my phone on even during sleep and someone from the other side used to watch over me for the whole night
note: TNM: a document named '24×7 Surveillance Rules & Regulations' with 70 points; held 28-30 Aug 2024, so a 47-hour REC timer is consistent (v1 row C51).

claim: A 76-year-old retired doctor in Hyderabad was held about 70 hours in digital arrest and later died of a heart attack (on-screen: 70 HOURS [MEDICAL DIALOGUES | SEPT 2025])
source_quote: suffered a heart attack after being kept under "digital arrest" for nearly 70 hours
note: Siasat 17 Sep 2025: died 8 Sep 2025 of cardiac arrest; police case includes culpable homicide after the family's complaint (v1 row C53). Not a suicide. The VO does not claim proven causation. Respectful visuals only.

claim: They threaten immediate arrest and the loss of your reputation and good name (on-screen: PILLAR 3 · TERROR)
source_quote: They threatened that an arrest would severely damage his reputation and career legacy.
note: ETV Bharat Telugu 21 Mar 2026: 'పరువు, ప్రతిష్ఠకు భంగం కలుగుతుందని భయపడి'.

claim: They give you no time to think; their weapon is your time
source_quote: And then their third move begins - the time pressure.
note: PM, Mann Ki Baat 27 Oct 2024 (IANS): 'In the midst of the conversation, you will not be able to even think.'

claim: To 'prove innocence' they demand money in a 'safe account', called an RBI account (on-screen: PILLAR 4 · MONEY · SIMULATION)
source_quote: transfer money to a fraudulent Reserve Bank of India (RBI) account
note: TNM on a Cambodian-run case. Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025 (Mangaluru DCP): deposit 'into a Reserve Bank of India (RBI) account for “verification.”' (v1 row C54).

claim: 'Secret supervision account' was the name used in Oswal's case
source_quote: a fake Supreme Court order asking him to release Rs 7 crore into a Secret Supervision Account (SSA)
note: Bar & Bench: 'directing him to release ₹7 crore into a Secret Supervision Account'.

claim: The RBI keeps no accounts for individuals and does not ask anyone to deposit money (so an 'RBI account' is fake)
source_quote: RBI does not maintain any account in the name of individuals/ companies/ trusts in India to hold funds for disbursal. It also does not open accounts for individuals or ask them to deposit money in those accounts.
note: RBI press release 2024-2025/998, 29 Aug 2024, which also names 'Digital Arrest'.

claim: Some victims are made to break fixed deposits (on-screen: ILLUSTRATION)
source_quote: మ్యూచువల్ ఫండ్స్, ఎఫ్డీలు బ్రేక్ చేయించి 7.12 కోట్ల రూపాయలు ట్రాన్స్‌ఫర్ చేయించుకున్నారు.
note: ETV Bharat Telugu 21 Mar 2026 (an 81-year-old in Hyderabad). Deccan Herald: a Bengaluru woman broke three FDs (v1 row C58).

claim: The promised return never happens
source_quote: when the promised refund did not materialise and the accused became unreachable
note: No report of scammers honouring a refund. Money comes back only through police freezes (e.g. Rs 5.25 crore of Oswal's Rs 7 crore).

claim: 'Digital arrest' does not exist in Indian law (on-screen: DIGITAL ARREST — NOT IN LAW [BNSS 2023 | RAJASTHAN HIGH COURT, JAN 2025])
source_quote: In fact, the recently enacted new criminal law does not provide for any legal provisions of conducting digital arrest.
note: Rajasthan High Court (Justice Anoop Kumar Dhand), Verdictum 24 Jan 2025. Telangana police (ETV Bharat Telugu 21 Mar 2026): 'న్యాయ వ్యవస్థలో అసలు డిజిటల్ అరెస్ట్ అనే పదమే లేదని తెలిపారు.' Tag correct.

claim: No law gives anyone the power to detain a person over a video call
source_quote: there is no provision for law enforcement to conduct 'arrest is via video-calls or online monitoring'
note: Same order. BNSS s.43(1): an arrest needs actual touch or confinement, or submission to custody.

claim: PM Modi in Mann Ki Baat (27 Oct 2024): there is no system like digital arrest in the law, it is fraud (on-screen: [MANN KI BAAT | 27 OCT 2024])
source_quote: I will reiterate that there is no system like digital arrest in the law, this is just a fraud, deceit, it is a lie
note: IANS via IBTimes: 'There is no system like digital arrest in the law, this is just fraud, deceit, lie'. MHA reply of 12 Mar 2025 confirms the date ('Mann Ki Baat' on 27.10.2024). The Telugu is a faithful condensed paraphrase.

claim: I4C advisory (Oct 2024): CBI, police, customs, ED and judges do not arrest anyone on a video call (on-screen: NO ARREST ON VIDEO CALL [I4C ADVISORY | OCT 2024])
source_quote: Don't Panic, Stay Alert. CBI/Police/Custom/ED/Judges DO NOT arrest you on video call,
note: Issued Saturday 5 Oct 2024; PTI via The Tribune, 7 Oct 2024: 'The CBI, ED, police, customs, or judges do not arrest people through video calls'.

claim: The BNSS is India's new criminal procedure law (on-screen: BNSS 2023)
source_quote: THE BHARATIYA NAGARIK SURAKSHA SANHITA, 2023 ... An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Criminal Procedure.
note: Gazette text (MHA). In force since 1 Jul 2024.

claim: BNSS s.43: the officer must actually touch or confine you, or you submit to custody (on-screen: 1 · PHYSICAL ARREST [BNSS S.43])
source_quote: In making an arrest the police officer or other person making the same shall actually touch or confine the body of the person to be arrested, unless there be a submission to the custody by word or action
note: Proviso: a woman's submission on oral intimation is presumed and only a female officer may touch her; the VO's 'or you submit to custody' covers it.

claim: BNSS s.36(a): the arresting officer's name must be clearly visible, like a name badge (on-screen: 2 · NAME VISIBLE [BNSS S.36])
source_quote: bear an accurate, visible and clear identification of his name which will facilitate easy identification;
note: D.K. Basu requirement (1): 'name togs [tags] with their designations'.

claim: BNSS s.36(b): an arrest memo made at the time of arrest, attested by a family member or a respectable local, and signed by you (on-screen: 3 · ARREST MEMO + WITNESS [BNSS S.36])
source_quote: Every police officer while making an arrest shall- ... prepare a memorandum of arrest which shall be- (i) attested by at least one witness, who is a member of the family of the person arrested or a respectable member of the locality where the arrest is made; (ii) countersigned by the person arrested; and
note: 'On the spot': s.36 applies 'while making an arrest'; D.K. Basu: 'memo of arrest at the time of arrest'.

claim: BNSS s.48: your relatives or a friend must be told at once of the arrest and where you are held (on-screen: 4 · FAMILY INFORMED [BNSS S.48])
source_quote: shall forthwith give the information regarding such arrest and place where the arrested person is being held to any of his relatives, friends or such other persons as may be disclosed or nominated by the arrested person
note: 'Forthwith' = immediately.

claim: You must be taken before a magistrate within 24 hours (on-screen: MAGISTRATE IN 24 H [BNSS S.58])
source_quote: such period shall not, in the absence of a special order of a Magistrate under section 187, exceed twenty-four hours exclusive of the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the Magistrate's Court
note: Journey time excluded; s.58 covers arrest without warrant, and Art. 22(2) of the Constitution gives the general rule (next rows).

claim: The name badge, arrest memo and informing family come from the Supreme Court's D.K. Basu judgment and are now in the law (on-screen: [D.K. BASU v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL | 1996])
source_quote: shall prepare a memo of arrest at the time of arrest a such memo shall be attested by atleast one witness.
note: Judgment of 18 Dec 1996 (reported (1997) 1 SCC 416); typos are the source's. Requirements (1)-(3): name tags, attested and countersigned memo, a friend or relative informed. Now BNSS ss.36 and 48 (PIB comparison, v1 row C71); Jurist (Aug 2026): 'The guidelines of Joginder Kumar and DK Basu remain in force.' Nuance: the inform-a-relative right was first laid down in Joginder Kumar v. State of U.P. (25 Apr 1994) and restated in D.K. Basu; 'came from D.K. Basu' is still fair.

claim: The 24-hour rule is in the Constitution (on-screen: 24 H [CONSTITUTION ART. 22(2)])
source_quote: Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest
note: Article 22(2), Constitution of India.

claim: The law says your family must be told; the scammer says hide it from your family (on-screen: LAW: TELL FAMILY · SCAM: HIDE FROM FAMILY)
source_quote: warned me not to disclose the matter to anyone, including my family
note: Law side: BNSS s.48 (row above).

claim: No police, court or RBI asks you to transfer money to prove innocence; a money demand means a scam (on-screen: MONEY DEMAND = SCAM [RBI · POLICE ADVISORIES])
source_quote: Police emphasised that there is no such thing as a digital arrest and that no law enforcement agency demands money to clear names or issue certificates.
note: Hyderabad police via Medical Dialogues (Sept 2025). Maharashtra CM (FPJ, 24 Feb 2026): no agency 'seeks money to settle legal issues'. RBI 29 Aug 2024: does not ask individuals to deposit money. PM, Mann Ki Baat: no government agency 'demands money on a video call'. Tag correct.

claim: Police booked the judge's case for cheating by personation, forgery and extortion (on-screen: BNS 319(2) · 338 · 308(2) · IT ACT 66C, 66D [TNM | MAR 2026])
source_quote: A case has been registered under Sections 316(2) (criminal breach of trust), 318(4) (cheating), 319(2) (cheating by personation), 338 (forgery of valuable securities, wills, or authority to transfer property), 308(2) (extortion) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) read with Section 66-C (identity theft) and 66-D (cheating by personation using computer resources) of the Information Technology (IT) Act.
note: The tag lists a correct subset; 316(2) and 318(4) are left out. OPTIONAL full tag: BNS 316(2) · 318(4) · 319(2) · 338 · 308(2) · IT ACT 66C, 66D [TNM | MAR 2026].

claim: One call to family or a friend can break the trap; the scheme depends on isolation
source_quote: Oswal approached the police after a senior member of one of his companies pointed out inconsistencies in the details of the case when he confided in them
note: Also the Mangaluru case (Deccan Herald 31 Oct 2025: she confided in a neighbour and police froze the money that evening; v1 row C52). MHA alert: victims 'remain visually available over Skype ... until their demands are met' (ETV Bharat).

claim: Don't call back numbers they give you; their own people answer
source_quote: The accused and the victim were then joined by another person on the call who claimed to be Circle Inspector Gourav Saradhi.
note: The 'officers' are part of the same gang. Deccan Herald 22 Dec 2024: a victim's call was 'transferred' to a fake police station (v1 row C77). Advice line.

claim: Don't install screen-share apps like AnyDesk (on-screen: NO APPS [RBI ALERT 1/2019 · NPCI])
source_quote: The Resrve Bank of India (RBI) has recently issued an advisory (Alert 1/2019) on February 14, pertaining to new modus operandi to commit fraud in digital payment ecosystem using remote screen access apps.
note: NPCI release reproduced by Outlook Business, 19 Feb 2019 ('Resrve' is the source's typo): 'Fraudster would lure the victim on some pretext to download an app called ‘AnyDesk’'. Tag correct for AnyDesk.

claim: ...or TeamViewer
source_quote: They ask them to install screen sharing apps such as Anydesk and TeamViewer in their mobile phones.
note: Gurugram police advisory (The Tribune, 24 Jan 2023). OPTIONAL tag: [RBI ALERT 1/2019 · NPCI · POLICE ADVISORIES].

claim: APK files sent on WhatsApp are a fraud tool: never install them
source_quote: Never download or install APK files or applications from unknown sources or links shared on WhatsApp, SMSes, or social media.
note: Hyderabad police advisory (Deccan Chronicle): 'Scammers are pushing malicious APK files through WhatsApp groups and messages.' ETV Bharat 24 Nov 2025 (Telangana): 'Cybercrime police are advising against opening these APK files.'

claim: Never share your OTP
source_quote: Police also told people not to share bank details, OTPs, or personal information with anybody.
note: Same advisory.

claim: The golden hour is the first hour; the faster you report, the better the chance of stopping the money (on-screen: THE GOLDEN HOUR [STATE CYBER ADVISORIES])
source_quote: Fadnavis stressed the concept of the golden hour, the first 60 minutes after a cyber fraud.
note: Maharashtra CM (FPJ, 24 Feb 2026): 'If victims report the incident within this time, there is a much higher chance of freezing or recovering the stolen money'. MHA official to ThePrint (18 Feb 2026): 'There is a golden hour, and if the money is blocked through prompt action, it can be saved'. Definitions vary: MP police say 'The first two hours in a cyber fraud case are considered the golden hour' (FPJ, 6 Jan 2026); the West Bengal CSCoE advisory could not be reached today. 'First hour' is the common usage; fine.

claim: 1930 is the national cybercrime helpline (on-screen: CALL 1930)
source_quote: A toll-free Helpline number '1930' has been operationalized to get assistance in lodging online cyber complaints.
note: MHA reply, 12 Mar 2025.

claim: Your complaint goes to the banks, asking them to freeze the accounts the money reached
source_quote: The ticket gets escalated to the concerned banks, Wallets and Merchants and so on. Depending on whether they are the victim's banks or the bank/wallet in which the defrauded money has gone.
note: Bank SOP on CFCFRMS (July 2026): 'If the defaulted money is still available, the Banks put it on hold'; the account is 'lien marked for the amount' or debit-frozen. Under MHA's Jan 2026 SOP the lien is normally limited to the disputed sum and a whole-account freeze is the exception (LiveLaw). OPTIONAL te: మీ కంప్లైంట్ బ్యాంకులకు వెళ్తుంది, డబ్బు చేరిన అకౌంట్స్ లో ఆ డబ్బుని హోల్డ్ చేయమని. en: Your complaint goes to the banks, asking them to put that money on hold in the accounts it reached.

claim: The system is called CFCFRMS
source_quote: The 'Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System', under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters.
note: MHA reply, 12 Mar 2025.

claim: To June 2026, over Rs 11,000 crore (Rs 11,158 crore) held across over 32 lakh (32.8 lakh) complaints (on-screen: ₹11,158 CR HELD · 32.8 LAKH COMPLAINTS · TO 30 JUN 2026 [MHA | LOK SABHA])
source_quote: Till June 30, 2026, a financial amount of more than ₹11,158 crore has been saved in more than 32.80 lakh complaints,
note: MoS Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar, written reply in the Lok Sabha (Tuesday, 11 Aug 2026), to PC Mohan MP; IANS via webindia123 has the same quote. 'Saved' means put on hold, not refunded: the SC order of 4 Aug 2026 records 'restoration completed in 36,290 cases for an aggregate amount of Rs. 18.05 crores'. Keep 'HELD (NOT ALL REFUNDED)'. OPTIONAL tag: [MHA REPLY, LOK SABHA | AUG 2026].

claim: So if you call fast, it really works
source_quote: If victims report the incident within this time, there is a much higher chance of freezing or recovering the stolen money,
note: Maharashtra CM, 24 Feb 2026; MHA official to ThePrint (golden hour).

claim: Call your bank and get the account blocked; file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in (on-screen: cybercrime.gov.in)
source_quote: On receipt of report of an unauthorised transaction from the customer, banks must take immediate steps to prevent further unauthorised transactions in the account.
note: RBI circular of 6 Jul 2017 (customers 'notify their bank ... at the earliest'). Portal: MHA reply 12 Mar 2025, 'National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal' (NCRP) (https://cybercrime.gov.in).

claim: Keep the evidence: screenshots, call logs, chats, transaction IDs
source_quote: if possible take a screenshot and record it for sure
note: PM, Mann Ki Baat 27 Oct 2024 (IANS). Advice line.

claim: If no money is lost yet, report the number on Chakshu (Sanchar Saathi) (on-screen: sancharsaathi.gov.in · CHAKSHU)
source_quote: Chakshu facilitates citizens to report the suspected fraud communications with the intention of defrauding telecom service users for cyber-crime, financial frauds, non-bonafide purpose like impersonation or any other misuse through Call, SMS or WhatsApp.
note: Same page lists 'impersonation as Government official' and says: 'If you have already lost money, please report at cyber crime helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.' Matches the script's order.

claim: Your one report could stop the next person's call
source_quote: Based on 7.7 lakh inputs provided by the citizens, 39.43 lakhs mobile connections have been disconnected
note: PIB, 5 Feb 2026 (MoS Communications, Rajya Sabha). DoT acts on the reports in aggregate, not one by one ('Rather than acting on individual reported suspected fraud communications, DoT uses the crowd sourced data'), so 'could stop' is the right hedge.

claim: Victims are already crushed inside after the loss
source_quote: డిజిటల్ అరెస్ట్ పేరుతో చేస్తున్న సైబర్ నేరాల్లో డబ్బు పోగొట్టుకున్న వృద్ధులు తీవ్రమైన మానసిక ఒత్తిడిలో ఉంటున్నారని పోలీసులు చెబుతున్నారు.
note: ETV Bharat Telugu, 21 Mar 2026 (police). Non-blaming framing matches the channel rule.

claim: Title: cyber cartels steal billions using fear
source_quote: generating just under US $40 billion in annual profits
note: Holds both ways: Rs 3,000+ crore (Rs 30+ billion) lost in India 2022-25 (V019 row), and just under US$40 billion a year in scam-centre profits regionally (UNODC).
